questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to improve my Arabic and learn more about the Middle East through cultural immersion, language exchange and experiences at a local university.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I improved my language skills immensely, got some very good new friends, and learned more about the region that I am focussing on in my studies at the University of Copenhagen.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy, given all the help provided by staff at my home institution.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received continuous support from my home institution whenever needed.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Some stuff was a little unclear, but in general the institution was very helpful whenever we needed help.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Use online Facebook groups.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It was very nice to meet friends outside of uni and I would definitely recommend living closer to the centre despite the bus ride every morning - for me it was really nice.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not use the university's housing, so I don't have additional comments.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very easy, again given the help from staff at my home institution.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I just sent an email and went to the office.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: A lot of help from the teachers

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was able to choose which class I wanted to be in and registration was easy.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just follow the advice of the teachers and you will be fine :)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I deliberately chose a level slightly above my own Arabic level, and I really enjoyed being challenged more and learn vocabulary relating to politics, conflict, war and economics.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: One of the teachers was talking a little too much about religion and her personal belief and she was very moralising. Nevertheless, I learned much more arabic from all of my teachers than I have learned at home and one of them had some very useful teaching mechanisms that KU could learn from.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Arabic for Non-Native Speakers (Level 5)

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Arabic for Non-Native Speakers (Level 5)

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Yes, but I got fed up with the sexism by the end.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Try to speak arabic from the beginning.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Sexism, religious fundamentalism, extreme politeness/attentiveness.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People's hospitality and welcoming attitudes.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1) Choose a high-level Arabic class with international students where all classes are in Arabic ONLY 2) Spend time at uni and don't be shy to speak Arabic to local students 3) Be prepared to face a lot of sexism (as a woman) on a daily basis and think about how you will deal with it.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No, I don't think so.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: That I improved my Arabic a lot and learned vocabulary so that I can now understand basic news and gain information from authentic media.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Dealing with the sexism and the moralising/disciplinary parts of the culture, especially since one of my teachers was always preaching the virtues of Islam, gender inequality etc. in class. In the end, it got a little too much. Also the favouring between students was very frustrating, and the fact that students could openly cheat in exams without the teacher sanctioning them.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Nope.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
